summary: Cabin on Morice Mountain near Houston, BC, built 1988 as a lookout; sources differ on whether fire watch or illegal burning was the main purpose. Shelter reported destroyed in September 2026.

facts.status_note: Shelter reported destroyed in the week before 25 Sep 2026. The hikers society said the walls were rotten and the wind likely brought it down.

staffing.status: no longer used for fire watch

access.note: Trail reopened in 2024 after the 2023 fire reroute, per Interior News. The hikers society says overnight stays are not recommended.

visit.trail_note: About 4.4 km trail, round trip about 5 hours per the hikers society. Trailhead moved about 800 m closer to town after the reroute. Overnight stays not recommended.

facts.agency: Recreation Sites and Trails BC, with Houston Hikers Society

events.note: Interior News and the hikers society both give 1988. Sources differ on the main purpose.
Northword says the Ministry of Forests decided to place a lookout observer on a knob near Houston, in the context of the 1988 build. The article does not give a separate staffing start date.
Northword says regulation changes under the new Forest Practices Code in 1994 removed the need to watch for illegal burning. It does not say the lookout closed that year.
Story Lookout trail first ribboned out in summer 2010 to reach the lookout.
2023 Peacock fire damaged the trail; the lower 1 km burned.
Trail reopened after the reroute. Interior News says reopened in 2024; the hikers society says the lower section was re-routed in late 2024.
Shelter reported destroyed in the week before 25 Sep 2026.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Interior News says it was built as a lookout for wildfire observers. Northword says the main reason was illegal burning, with wildfire watch as an added benefit. The story gives both.
Interior News says the trail reopened in 2024. The hikers society says the lower section was re-routed in late 2024. The story reports both dates.
Interior News spells the name Storey once in its text. Other sources use Story. Northword ties the name to Marge Storey.

notes_for_editor: The provincial Sites and Trails BC page listed in source_pages (REC262283) and the trail page REC262281 returned no text on fetch, so neither is cited. The 2026 loss rests on one news report; no later account or photo was found. The Northword PDF gives no date, so the 'five years ago' refurbishment is not dated. No height or construction details were found; height_m is omitted. Brief status 'unknown' is replaced with 'destroyed' per Interior News, which describes the shelter as gone. The 1988 'staffed_first' event is inferred from the Northword sentence about placing an observer; treat it as approximate. The site may be worth a recheck after the rebuild plans are reported.
